summary.text: The normal force is the part of a contact force that pushes perpendicular to the surface an object touches.
It is what stops a person standing on a platform from sinking through it, by resisting the pull of gravity.
A bathroom scale reads the normal force, which is why its reading changes when an elevator accelerates.

facts.label: Standing still
facts.value: Normal force equals weight in size

items.prompt: You stand on a bathroom scale in an elevator that speeds upward. Why does the reading go up?

options.label: Gravity pulls harder on you while you move upward
Your mass really grows as the elevator accelerates
The scale reads the normal force, which exceeds your weight then
The scale reads only your weight, which is unchanged

items.explain: The scale measures normal force, which varies as the cab accelerates, not gravitational force.

items.prompt: A book rests on a table. A student says its weight and the table's push on it are an action-reaction pair. What is wrong with that?

options.label: They are an action-reaction pair, so nothing is wrong
The table is not actually pushing back at all
The weight is always larger than the table's push
They are equal only because the book is not accelerating

items.explain: Treating them as a pair is a common mistake; they need to be equal in size to explain why there is no upward acceleration.

items.prompt: A ball bounces upward off the floor. During the bounce, how does the normal force compare with the ball's weight?

options.label: It is larger, which gives the upward acceleration
It is smaller, which lets the ball rise
It is equal, since the floor does not move
It is zero, since the ball has left the floor

items.explain: A ball that accelerates upward has a normal force larger in size than its weight.

items.prompt: On a spinning amusement ride, riders stay pinned to the wall with the floor gone. What holds them up?

options.label: The floor beneath them dropping more slowly
Friction with the wall, produced by the wall's push on them
A strong upward pull from the ride's motor
Gravity weakening as the ride spins faster

items.explain: The wall applies a normal force toward the center, and static friction resulting from it counteracts gravity.

items.prompt: A geometry teacher says a line is normal to a surface. How does she mean "normal"?

options.label: Ordinary or expected
Running alongside it
Perpendicular to it
Equal in length to it

items.explain: In this context normal is used in the geometric sense and means perpendicular, not "ordinary".

items.prompt: Why can't the atoms of your hand pass through a table?

options.label: A hidden glue holds every surface together
Atoms are solid balls that cannot be squeezed
The table is always heavier than a hand
Electrons at the two surfaces cannot overlap without a big energy cost

items.explain: The normal force results from the interactions of electrons at the surfaces; their wavefunctions cannot overlap without large energy.
